market.state: UPTREND INTACT - OPENING INTO A ROTATION, NOT A TOP
market.advice: Going into the open the index is fine and the leadership is not. SPY sits at 767.45, 1.3% off its high and comfortably above a rising 50-day at 749.53; QQQ at 717.51 also holds its 50-day; the distribution-day count is still zero and VIX at 15.8 is calm even though it is drifting up against a 15.1 five-day average. Nothing in that describes a market that is breaking. What is breaking is who leads. Breadth has slipped to 56% of the 451 scanned names above their 50-day, and the sector table is unambiguous: Energy has 16 of its 20 names on a STRONG BUY signal (80%), Financials 32 of 56 and Healthcare 27 of 52, while Utilities manage 1 of 33 and Communication Services 1 of 10. Technology, the sector that led for a year, converts only 29 of 79. Two forces did this and both are still live at the open. The Strait of Hormuz remains shut - Iran says it stays that way until Washington meets interim-deal conditions, Trump says no talks are planned or scheduled, and crude printed a three-week high overnight. That is a direct bid under every producer, refiner and midstream name. Separately, Treasury yields surged, and that is what actually did the damage: it pulled Wall Street to two-week lows led by tech and it detonated the AI-power complex, which is why Utilities is the single worst-scoring group on this scan. TradingView's independent read confirms the rotation rather than arguing with it. Of the 113 names it rated, 28 came back SELL and 3 STRONG SELL - COIN, LUV and NXPI - and almost every one of those is a semiconductor, a crypto proxy or a high-multiple software name. All 13 of its STRONG BUYs sit in energy, defense, insurance and large-cap pharma: TRGP, APA, OXY, OKE, EOG, RTX, HWM, SAIC, LLY, JNJ, AMGN, DXCM and ELV. Two independent methods, same answer. The plan for this session is to participate in the rotation but to be fussy about entry, because the new leadership has already run. Buy the un-extended names inside it rather than the vertical ones. EOG is the single best-shaped chart on the scan - a fresh 52-week high reached with an RSI of only 53.5, which means the advance is being built rather than blown off - while VLO at RSI 79.3 and 22% above its 50-day, and MPC at RSI 76.1 and 25.6% above its, are the same trade after the easy part. Size the energy weighting as a headline position, not a fundamental one: the whole group is priced off a waterway that could reopen on one sentence from Tehran, so buy it as if a single paragraph can take back a week. In financials, rising yields are a tailwind rather than a tax, but JPM at RSI 78.2, SCHW at 86.7 and NTRS at 86.5 are stretched; the money is in RGA at 8.3x forward with EPS up 159.6%, in MET at RSI 51.4, and in PNC and CFG, all of which are within 3% of their highs without being overbought. Healthcare is the second green corner and the cleanest one, because LLY and JNJ are making highs with RSI in the fifties. On the other side, the oversold mega-cap technology that just got sold is not automatically broken, but it is a support test rather than a breakout: AAPL opens at 310.03 with an RSI of 28.2 sitting directly on a rising 50-day at 308.90, and it either holds that line today or it does not - which is why it is a WATCH here and not a buy, and why TradingView rates it only NEUTRAL. Avoid the AI-power utilities entirely while yields are rising; that trade is fighting its multiple and its cost of capital at the same time. Keep normal position sizing, respect that 44% of the universe is now below its 50-day, and let the extended names come to you rather than chasing the gap.

picks.thesis: NEW LISTING - judge this on the business, not the signals. SpaceX has only weeks of trading history, so the 52-week, VCP and relative-strength readings that drive every other name on this list are structurally unavailable, and TradingView will not resolve a rating for it yet. What is real: the price sits at 143.34, roughly 1% above its short 50-day and about 32% below its post-listing high, having found a floor near 108. That is a normal IPO give-back finding a level. The investment case is a launch-cadence and Starlink-subscription franchise with no credible Western competitor, priced at whatever the public market decides a formerly private asset is worth - which is exactly why it is a WATCH: the business is extraordinary and the price discovery is not finished.
